report_redefined_cv replaces an existing non-constant CV not marked as a method.

warn_elem_scalar_context shows an undef or unknown-expression placeholder for a hash element accessed with aggregate sigil in scalar context. Preserve composed name/bracket arguments. Preserve WARN_SYNTAX and existing delivery behavior.

The same helper reports a single-element slice in scalar context using an undef or unknown-key placeholder. Keep slice and hash-sigil forms distinct. Preserve WARN_SYNTAX and existing delivery behavior.

warn_elem_scalar_context has a constant key value, pretty-printing strings before displaying the scalar-sigil suggestion. This differs from its placeholder input contract. Preserve WARN_SYNTAX and existing delivery behavior.
The slice form uses a known constant key value and the corresponding scalar-sigil suggestion. Preserve its SV formatter and composed arguments. Preserve WARN_SYNTAX and existing delivery behavior.
new_ctype finds characters whose classification/case behavior conflicts with Perl expectations and accumulates the list, count, locale type and optional codeset for locale-warning delivery.

is_safe_syscall rejects a NUL before the final supplied byte, sets ENOENT and reports both sides of the NUL. A trailing terminator is allowed. This validates syscall arguments, not Unicode encoding. Keep the controlling warning category and all delivery variants.
The wide-locale macros report a code point under non-UTF-8 CTYPE, preserving operation context and WARN_LOCALE policy.

scan_version component accumulation and upg_version numeric input validation report overflow with VERSION_MAX as the displayed value, not the original overflowing input. Preserve that payload and saturation behavior. Keep existing warning control and all emitter variants.

scan_version detects overflow in component multiplication/addition and saturates at VERSION_MAX without a displayed limit parameter. Keep the distinct parameter contract. Keep existing warning control and all emitter variants.

upg_version warns when SCAN_VERSION leaves an unconsumed suffix. The earlier invalid-input error remains a separate contract. WARN_MISC controls its warning class; subject tags retain the operation family.
Perl_vnumify warns under WARN_NUMERIC when the verified version object has an alpha marker. Numification discards development-version semantics; this is not a floating-point precision warning.
The platform DynaLoader backend receives the global-symbol flag but uses its historical unsupported-global warning path. Preserve literal filenames and backend behavior.
OS2 pthread_join receives the sentinel thread ordinal for a failed start, distinct from the separate fatal invalid-ordinal check.

OS2 Deregister_MQ expects PM mode before restoring the initial program mode but sees another mode.
OS2 DevCap closes its temporary screen context when called without a supplied context and reports DevCloseDC failure.
OS2 fork resource restoration fails DosQueryModuleName for a module loaded in the parent and skips reloading that entry.
OS2 fork resource restoration fails DosLoadModule for a previously loaded DLL and reports the loader-provided problematic module.
VMemNL::Free finds a block owned by another nonnull pool, reports the two pools and deliberately faults for a stack trace.
Inline g/o modifiers are warned once per direction/context according to wastedflags. The enabled/disabled selector and syntax prefix remain intact.
Inline c has a separate once-only warning and guidance from g/o. Preserve its enabled/disabled selector and literal syntax prefix.
Inline -p cannot turn off keep-copy behavior, so the parser reports its no-effect status.
Strict regex parsing encounters an empty (?) modifier group before the ordinary modifier parser.
regpiece finds max < min for a counted quantifier, warns and emits OPFAIL. This differs from an out-of-range or malformed integer.
A non-greedy suffix follows a counted quantifier with equal minimum and maximum; the suffix cannot change its count.
regpiece sees a non-postponed zero-width atom with a maximum above REG_INFTY/3, warns and limits pointless repetition. This is not Perl subroutine recursion.
A braced Unicode boundary escape under /a or /aa requires Unicode boundary rules. The warning preserves the original ASCII modifier spelling and boundary span.

The shared alien-digit builder records an invalid digit, original escape and suggested resolved spelling. Regex atom and bracket-class octal paths append pattern context afterwards. Preserve its radix selector.
The regex literal-atom scanner warns on an unrecognized alphanumeric escape unless the following brace is about to produce its own error.
Non-strict regex parsing treats a non-quantifier { as literal where the context is ambiguous. Strict/prohibited contexts use the separate error identity.
Strict regex scanning warns about an unescaped } or ] in a literal run. The actual delimiter character remains structured data.

Regex atom and character-class compilation report native-Unicode values beyond Unicode under WARN_PORTABLE, guarded by warning-position and nonportable-suppression rules. Preserve regex-location delivery. Keep existing warning control and all emitter variants.
add_above_Latin1_folds requests inverse folds and finds none for a folded codepoint. The producer is regex class folding; retain WARN_REGEXP despite its older deprecated-warning comment.
The bracket parser recognizes POSIX-looking contents without their required additional outer brackets. Selectors retain recognized, invalid and unimplemented POSIX interpretations.
A named escape in a bracket class resolves to zero codepoints in non-strict processing and contributes nothing.
A multicharacter named escape is not representable under the current single-character, inverted or range constraints. The non-strict path warns and uses its first codepoint.

An extended set requests an inversion list from a mixed codepoint/string property. Codepoint data can be used, but the string part is not supported and is warned about. String-only properties use an error.
Non-strict bracket-class parsing warns for an unknown ASCII alphanumeric escape; strict parsing throws its existing class error.
regclass sees literal vertical whitespace under double-extended mode without enhanced_xx. The enhanced feature path is a separate fatal error.
regclass sees unescaped hash under double-extended mode without enhanced_xx. This is regexp character-class grammar, not object fields.

Strict parsing sees a below-256 endpoint with explicit Unicode notation and a nonportable other endpoint. It warns about mixed endpoint interpretation.
Strict parsing finds a printable ASCII endpoint but nonportable notation or endpoints that are not both digits or same-case ASCII letters.
Strict Unicode digit-range checking finds endpoints in different decimal digit groups, including its adjacent-group inverse-list special handling.

Comment scanning sees a later unquoted, unescaped nonterminal hash and suggests escaping or quoting it. This is a warning, not a Note-class leaf.
Comment scanning in bracket-class context sees an unquoted, unescaped closing bracket, which remains part of the comment instead of closing the class.
study_chunk finds nonzero lookbehind length variation with a capture CLOSE and suppresses restudy warnings. Positive/negative text, location delivery and warn-once policy are preserved.
The retained deprecate compatibility macro forwards a supplied component message and warning category to this generic catalog diagnostic. No current direct C producer calls the wrapper.
The retained deprecate_disappears_in compatibility macro forwards a component message, removal version and warning category. No current direct C producer calls the wrapper.

XS_builtin_func1_void accepts the registered weaken/unweaken opcode indices; its default rejects another dispatcher index. Keep it distinct from the scalar dispatcher contract.

The shared \c helper rejects { when its toCTRL result is nonprintable on the current platform. The printable-result variant has separate display data.
The shared \c helper rejects { while recording its printable control result for the platform-specific explanatory template.
The four deprecated grok_bslash entry points deliberately throw regardless of input. Record the escape API subject without changing the deferred compatibility-wrapper policy.
The shared octal escape scanner rejects UV overflow or UV_MAX when its caller disallows that sentinel. Preserve the radix-specific identity and parser return index.
pending_ident rejects package-qualified my/state/field variable or subroutine names, separately from the our qualifier diagnostic.

review_status: applied; Compilation and Phase producer-contract review
rationale: The parser adds its source context to a legacy opaque diagnostic; context selection remains structured.

Lexer and parser error paths append a possible runaway-string suggestion with delimiter and start-line data. Its association is not guaranteed, so preserve the independently controlled warning and compatibility layout. Preserve WARN_SYNTAX and existing delivery behavior.
The name helper rejects an empty trimmed name or appends an unknown-name diagnostic when constant-handler resolution fails without already recording its own error.
For a non-core handler, the helper validates the name start and continuation characters in native-byte and UTF8 forms and marks the bad source span.
Non-core handler input-name validation finds adjacent ASCII spaces and marks their source span. This is distinct from general invalid name characters.

A user charnames handler returns an SV flagged UTF8 whose bytes fail validation. Keep it in UTF8 and retain both the escape context and valid value prefix. This is returned-value validation, not malformed input-name spelling.

Regex runtime name lookup appends a pattern-position wrapper after the shared helper fails, adopts diagnostics since entry and throws the complete exception. Preserve containment and standalone location rendering.
The UTF8 encoder range helper formats the rejected codepoint in hexadecimal and reports MAX_LEGAL_CP. Preserve its source callers and no-return behavior.
The regex compiler rejects a named U+ sequence or a class endpoint above MAX_LEGAL_CP, retaining its special UV_MAX range sentinel handling and regex position.

warn_expect_operator finds a token where an operator is required, records nearby parser context and chooses nested Note hints under the same WARN_SYNTAX guard. Preserve warning grouping and fallback-token selectors. Preserve WARN_SYNTAX and existing delivery behavior.
S_warn_expect_operator selects this suggestion for the first token of a statement, under the parent WARN_SYNTAX diagnostic. It is a nested hint, not an independently controlled warning.
The missing-operator scanner suggests predeclaration only when the preceding token is an identifier followed by whitespace. Preserve its shared WARN_SYNTAX control and nested hint role.

The missing-operator scanner appends this context-specific suggestion when neither first-token semicolon nor predeclaration heuristics apply. Preserve the UTF-8 context parameter and parent association.
The C3 merge has nonempty candidate sequences but no legal head winner. This is a user-definable inconsistent hierarchy, not necessarily internal corruption.
On C3 merge failure, each class already present in the partial result is appended as structured context. Its existing severity and grouping are preserved.
On the same C3 failure, the final candidate parent is recorded as failure context. It is part of the same ordered diagnostic group.
The mro_set_mro XS entry point asks gv_stashsv with GV_ADD to create or find the package, then rejects a null result before accessing MRO metadata. This does not instantiate an object.
The next-method extension exhausts subroutine contexts and stack levels without finding a usable method context. This is a primary call-context error, not a hint or a count bound.

While finding the enclosing next-method context, the extension cannot obtain a fully qualified subroutine name containing the package separator. Preserve its separate failure from exhausting all method contexts.
The next-method extension finds no later implementation in either its negative cache or the actual MRO search when throw_nomethod is enabled. Optional next::can lookup can instead return empty.

diag_error_hook_value appends this hint only to a copied delivery view when further groups remain. The canonical caught exception is not changed, and the annotation does not independently trigger warn or die.
S_reg requires a matching closing parenthesis for a group. Extended-character-class fence completion also uses this identity for an unmatched grouping parenthesis.
Both regatom and regclass require a closing bracket for a bracket class; a trailing escape inside the class also selects this diagnostic.
At top-level pattern completion S_reg encounters an unpaired closing parenthesis.

S_reg scans the (*...) construct name and optional colon argument and requires a closing parenthesis. Existing selectors distinguish upper-case named verbs from generic constructs and argument versus construct truncation.
S_reg compares compilation recursion depth against four times the configured RE_COMPILE_RECURSION_LIMIT. This is parser nesting, not user recursion during a match.
S_reg sees pattern whitespace between the opening parenthesis and star. Its selector preserves the historical upper-case verb versus generic construct wording.
reg_scan_name makes no identifier progress at the group name start and reports the requirement for an initial nondigit word character.
After all parentheses have been counted, reg_scan_name cannot find the requested name in RExC_paren_names. Earlier passes defer forward names.
S_reg finds ignored pattern whitespace between ( and ? in the indivisible (? opener token.
The (?P< capture-name or (?P> subroutine-name prefix ends at the pattern boundary before any name content. Its selector preserves which form was intended.
parse_lparen_question_flags exhausts the pattern before reaching the colon or close parenthesis ending an inline modifier group.
After scanning the named subroutine target of (?&NAME) or (?P>NAME), the compiler requires a closing parenthesis.
Named capture scanning requires its matching angle or quote delimiter after the identifier and preserves the opener as data.
S_reg scans a quoted or angle-delimited named condition and requires its matching closing name delimiter.
The empty-positive and empty-negative lookaround handling paths skip ignored text and detect pattern end before closure.

Numeric subroutine calls and backreferences reject nonexistent absolute or relative group targets, deferring forward targets until all groups are counted. The identity spans both call and backreference producers.
Numeric subroutine-call parsing rejects numeric scanner failure, I32 overflow and relative-to-absolute index overflow.
Inline modifier parsing reaches excess_modifier with ASCII restriction already set and rejects a further a. The existing single-character parameter remains.
Inline charset parsing reaches excess_modifier with the same previous and current non-a flag, rejecting repetition.
Inline charset parsing rejects a second different charset mode. This is distinct from source-literal parser accumulation and retains regex-position data.
Charset modifier branches reject placement after the minus separator. Ordinary negatable modifiers such as m remain allowed.
Regex named-character, boundary and property escape parsing requires a closing brace and retains the escape letter as data.
After trimming allowed blanks and property inversion syntax, a braced boundary/property escape has no content.
handle_regex_sets parses an interpolated parenthesized value and requires exactly one REGEX_SET node, not an arbitrary regex or extra nodes.
At expression completion the set evaluator requires exactly one operand inversion list and an empty remainder stack. Empty fenced groups also branch to this error.
The extended-class parse loop reaches the pattern end without a complete closing construct. Preserve its current generic syntax-error wording.
handle_operand finds consecutive operands without an intervening set operator, respecting the current parenthesis fence.
The set evaluator finds an invalid binary-operator stack position, or a non-unary operator where the operand handler permits only !. This is set expression grammar, not Perl arithmetic.
The set-token switch accepts no operator or operand form for the current nonterminal character.
After completing the set expression a closing square bracket is not immediately followed by the required parenthesis.
A closing parenthesis appears without a matching fence and is not the final ) following ].
The evaluator rejects an opening parenthesis where its operator/operand stack and fence require a different token.

get_quantifier_value sees grok_atoUV failure with a leading zero and preserves the historical invalid-quantifier message. Overflow and too-large values take 2556. The existing numeric-scanner follow-up is separate.
get_quantifier_value rejects values at or above REG_INFTY or numeric overflow and reports REG_INFTY-1 as the supported bound.
After compiling one quantified atom and optional greediness/possessive suffix, regpiece finds another quantifier.
regatom encounters ?, + or * where no preceding atom exists for quantification.
Recognized colon-taking (*...) lookaround/verb constructs branch to no_colon when their required colon is absent.
The (*...) name dispatch leaves op unset. Upper-case/empty names use named-verb wording and lower-case names use generic construct wording, through existing selectors.
A recognized construct marked arg_required has no nonempty argument after parsing. The code preserves the actual construct name.
Property-wildcard inline parsing rejects disabling m, enabling s/g and charset modes other than required aa. The sign and flag data remain separate from the sentence.

Inline-modifier parsing, unknown (?P...) forms and malformed (??...) constructs share the unrecognized-sequence template with their literal sequence prefix. Preserve these multiple grammar entry points.
Named backreference delimiters and malformed numeric \g{...} closure use the same sequence-not-terminated diagnostic, retaining the literal escape/construct prefix.
Strict regex parsing and prohibited ambiguous alphabetic-escape contexts reject an unescaped { that is not a quantifier. Non-strict warning paths remain distinct.
regclass sees \p or \P at the pattern end before any short name or braced form.
A property escape without braces is followed by a nonalphabetic character rather than a supported short property name.
A relative backreference resolves to a group index below one. The legacy wording also describes an unavailable/unclosed target.
The backref number helper returns its invalid sentinel with no leading digit, selecting unterminated-reference rather than nonexistent-numeric-target wording.
A numeric braced backreference lacks its ending brace after the scanned digits, before ordinary name handling can resolve it.
A numeric backreference resolves to zero. Whole-pattern recursion uses separate (?0) syntax and does not make group-zero backreferences valid.
The engine parses the frozen/runtime \N{U+...} sequence with grok_hex and rejects an empty numeric token or invalid separator content.
Regex \N has a following brace only after ignored /x text. Unlike bare \N, a named escape requires the opening brace immediately.
In a bracket class, grok_bslash_N reports the bare/non-name form through a negative cp_count. A named escape is required in this position.

Strict bracket-class parsing cannot represent a multi-character named sequence under single-character-only, inverted or range restrictions. Non-strict handling retains its warning and first-character compatibility.
grok_bslash_N recognizes the tokenizer-produced \N{_} marker for an empty named sequence and rejects it under strict parsing. Non-strict mode retains zero-count semantics.
After compiling the conditional first branch, an alternation separator is rejected specifically for DEFINE. Normal conditionals may have an else branch.
After the conditional body and optional else branch, S_reg reaches pattern end instead of a closing parenthesis.
After consuming the permitted conditional alternatives, a further non-closing token remains before pattern end, producing the excess-branch diagnostic.
S_reg rejects an invalid/out-of-range numeric test or a recognized test whose required closing parenthesis is absent. Shared insert_if_check_paren paths mean this is not exclusively numeric syntax.
The (? construct dispatch reaches its NUL case before receiving a complete group type.
No recognized named, numeric, recursion or assertion condition handler accepts the condition prefix.
The only producer rejects \G in a property-wildcard pattern. Other anchor escapes have special wildcard semantics rather than sharing this prohibition.
regatom permits \K outside lookaround but rejects it while RExC_in_lookaround is true. The restriction belongs to assertion contents.
regatom explicitly rejects the uppercase \C escape. Lowercase \c control escapes use a separate shared parser.
regpiece rejects a property-wildcard quantifier whose minimum is zero and maximum is unbounded. This restriction limits unnecessary expensive wildcard matching.
Property-wildcard regex parsing rejects a nested \p or \P property escape before resolving its property contents.
A named class is used as a range endpoint. Strict mode throws this error; the existing non-strict path warns and treats the dash literally.
The end codepoint precedes the start codepoint. The EBCDIC Unicode-range path also compares converted Latin-1 endpoint ordering. Preserve the original range span.
regclass strict mode rejects literal vertical whitespace when skip_white is false. Extended-xx deprecation behavior outside that branch is unchanged.
Strict bracket-class parsing scans up to four octal digits and requires exactly three in its legacy unbraced octal form. Non-strict ill-digit warnings are separate.
An unrecognized ASCII alphanumeric escape in regclass is fatal in strict mode. Non-strict mode uses the separate existing warning; escaped punctuation such as underscore is accepted.
Despite the old EXPECTING_CLOSE_BRACKET code, S_reg checks for ) after a numeric relative/absolute subroutine-call specification. This is group-reference syntax and has no character-class producer.
The (?+ prefix is not followed by a nonzero digit, so no positive relative subroutine-call number can be parsed. Negative prefixes may instead enter inline flag parsing.
regatom completes a literal run and detects that its unsigned STRLEN does not fit its signed IV check. Preserve the current conversion and regex-location reporting.
regatom reaches a branch/group terminator without TRYAGAIN; callers should have handled it before requesting another atom.
The reserved (?$...) and (?@...) group-type branches are explicitly unimplemented. The type character remains a semantic parameter.
parse_ident_msg rejects group-name identifier syntax. reg_scan_name retains reason-kind selector, codepoint and identifier spans before appending pattern location data.
The braced \b/\B boundary escape name is not one of the accepted grapheme/line/sentence/word boundary spellings. Bound meant boundary here, not a quantifier bound.
handle_possible_posix recognizes a syntactically valid but unknown POSIX class name outside check-only mode. Its selector preserves complemented versus positive spelling.
A fully formed [=...=] or [. ... .] reserved POSIX construct reaches the reserved-syntax path with no earlier problem and not in check-only mode.
regclass is returning an inversion list for an extended set, but the Unicode property provides only strings and no codepoint definition. Mixed properties take a separate warning.
Outside the explicit multi-character class mechanism, a string-valued property cannot be inverted by class inversion xor uppercase P.

handle_possible_posix appends reason-selector diagnostics speculatively. The caller may discard the entire group after ruling out a POSIX interpretation. Preserve speculative rollback and attached regex location.
parse_ident reports the offending codepoint and source spans when identifier validation finds an invalid character. Check-only callers receive failure details instead of throwing.
parse_ident reports numeric special-variable names with forbidden leading zeros. Check-only callers retain their nonthrowing failure result.

UNTOGGLE_NUMERIC rejects an LC_NUMERIC restoration when its nesting depth is already zero or negative. It does not mean a libc locale switch returned failure.
bool_setlocale_2008_i duplicates special or rollback locale objects before modifying categories. A null duplocale result prevents safe state preservation.
Both LC_ALL update callers require full_array after reparsing a previously accepted name with array filling enabled. The other parser return states violate that contract.
Windows locale initialization, sync, thread switching and localeconv setup/teardown reject the error result from _configthreadlocale. Preserve every platform-guarded producer.
The POSIX 2008 global-switch macro requires uselocale(LC_GLOBAL_LOCALE) to succeed before freeing thread-local locale objects.
init_i18nl10n cannot create the process-wide POSIX C locale object with newlocale. It releases the initialization lock before reporting the failure.
The initialization fallback loop advances past dummy_trial before its switch; encountering that sentinel is an internal trial-state error, not an invalid user locale name.
CRNCYSTR emulation requires my_localeconv to populate p_cs_precedes along with the currency symbol; the expected hash entry is absent.
The category-to-index helper cannot map a libc category and its caller did not request a nonthrowing succeeded result. Preserve its valid failure-return form.
posix_LC_foo receives an unsupported CC_* classification or case-mapping number. It unlocks LC_CTYPE before the panic. This is not a user regexp class-name failure.
toggle_locale_i must query the current category name before recording how to restore it. A null query result is an internal locale-state failure.
my_localeconv accepts zero for all fields or one of its supported langinfo item constants. An unsupported nonzero item reaches the default switch arm.
Windows switch_locale_context enables per-thread locale mode and then cannot restore the saved LC_ALL name. Keep the saved-name parameter and later cleanup.
Initialization, interpreter switching and thread setup cannot activate the required locale object with uselocale. Preserve the object pointer and expected LC_ALL name.
bool_setlocale_2008_i successfully constructs the requested new locale but cannot activate it. The object is freed before the panic and the caller line is retained.
LC_ALL parsing in check_that_overridden mode verifies that a category configured as ignored was already represented by its required override. Preserve the expected/actual category strings.

Locale startup fails its initial setting attempt and renders the setup warning before listing environment settings. This helper constructs text rather than a diagnostic object.

Locale startup formats each tried fallback into a string before the enclosing failure summary is output. This RENDER entry creates no diagnostic and preserves fallback/standard/system selectors.
Locale startup exhausts fallback attempts and renders the preserved locale list and count, with language-specific plural selection.
Locale startup renders the successful fallback kind and name, including the explicit unknown-name case, without creating a warning record.
Windows and Amiga pseudo-child run loops receive restart jump code 3 without PL_restartop. Keep direct formatting and status cleanup rather than adding exception allocation.

Diagnostic::derive rejects a replacement child whose descendant graph contains the original receiver. This is the current conservative graph contract.
DiagGroup::children, child_count and append require the stored children/messages field to resolve to an AV reference, including after caller mutations.
DiagGroup append rejects a proposed child graph containing the parent, using the visited-node traversal rather than a depth limit.
The ordinary DiagGroup append path rejects a child not derived from Diagnostic. Exception-specific calls retain their distinct legacy API wording.
Exception append and record_throw reject non-Diagnostic message values. They share this diagnostic rather than silently wrapping arbitrary payloads.
Perl_xperl_object_hv requires a blessed hash reference derived from the requested receiver class. The class parameter identifies the actual method receiver contract.
An explicit render context must be a hash reference. The active-ancestor marker slot also checks that its caller-visible stored value remains a hash reference.
Diagnostic::_new requires a hash reference for its fields argument before fetching metadata.
Diagnostic::_new rejects undef and empty string codes after stringification; it does not validate arbitrary nonempty user codes against catalog membership.
Diagnostic::_new requires an AV reference for the params field and copies that array. This guard does not validate each parameter hash.
A defined location supplied to Diagnostic::_new must be a hash reference; omitted location becomes an empty hash.
A defined warning_categories field must be an array reference before copying. Warning-category policy is not changed here.
Diagnostic::_new rejects references for a defined light flag. The compatibility flag is retained during this classification work.

Diagnostic::_new rejects a reference, nonnumeric context_follows_index or a negative integer conversion. Preserve the current numeric acceptance behavior; fractional/infinite index validation needs a separate contract review.
Exception::record_throw requires a hash reference for the throw event.
record_throw rejects any caller-provided message_index key, even undef. The exception sets this field after appending the supplied diagnostic.
A throw event whose reason string is rethrow requires a defined accompanying diagnostic before append/type validation.

Diagnostic::render accepts only the legacy format name and rejects other names. Modern and JSON/Dumper rendering use separate methods. Preserve its current argument-count behavior during this classification.
